hunks.baseline: But that brief moment, flashing past like a bolt of lightning, could feel like ten years to someone caught inside it.
hunks.sol: But a moment that flashed past like lightning could feel like ten years to someone caught inside it.

hunks.baseline: Why hadn’t the palm he’d instinctively thrust out toppled his opponent just before those beastlike teeth sank into his neck?
hunks.sol: Why hadn’t the palm strike he’d thrown on instinct brought his opponent down before those beastlike teeth sank into his neck?

hunks.baseline: Why was the Murim Alliance’s banner flying over the heads of those damn bandits?
hunks.sol: Why was the Murim Alliance’s banner flying above those damn bandits?

hunks.baseline: And as he felt his body, no longer under his control, being pushed helplessly backward, he muttered to himself:
hunks.sol: As he felt his body slip beyond his control and fall helplessly backward, he thought:

hunks.baseline: Lying in a pool of blood like a pond, the Blood Lord suddenly looked up at the sky filling his vision.
hunks.sol: Lying in a pool of blood as broad as a pond, the Blood Lord looked up at the sky filling his vision.

hunks.baseline: The monster’s pupils were still as red as blood, but even now, his fading gaze could no longer make out light from shadow.
hunks.sol: The monster’s eyes were still as red as blood, but his fading sight could no longer distinguish light from shadow.

hunks.baseline: A world entirely gone black.
hunks.sol: A world gone entirely black.

hunks.baseline: Beyond it, the only things the Blood Lord could feel were the relentless rain pouring down and the chill of blood soaking his entire body.
hunks.sol: Beyond it, all the Blood Lord could feel was the rain pouring down without pause and the chill of blood soaking his body.

hunks.baseline: No. Those weren’t the only things.
hunks.sol: No. That wasn’t all.

hunks.baseline: Someone’s voice rang in his ears like an echo.
hunks.sol: Someone’s voice echoed in his ears.

hunks.baseline: He spat out the flesh and blood that had filled his mouth and smiled.
hunks.sol: He spat out the flesh and blood filling his mouth and smiled, though he was panting as if he might collapse at any moment. Even forcing out one syllable at a time looked like a struggle.

hunks.baseline: Even as he panted like he was about to collapse.
Even with a face that looked as though it took all he had just to force out each syllable.
“I can hear you. Crystal clear, too.”
hunks.sol: “I can hear it. Clear as day.”

hunks.baseline: He could only swallow the blood and phlegm bubbling up in his throat and listen to the roar shaking the heavens and earth.
hunks.sol: He could only swallow the bloody phlegm rising in his throat and listen to the roar shaking heaven and earth.

hunks.baseline: We shall destroy evil and set the heavens right.
hunks.sol: Destroy demons and set Heaven right.

hunks.baseline: It was the old Murim Alliance’s banner, the vow it had upheld to the very end—and the hoof that had trampled its invaders.
hunks.sol: It was the old Murim Alliance’s rallying cry, the oath it had upheld to the very end—and the hoof that trampled the invaders.

hunks.baseline: But he could picture it just by listening.
hunks.sol: But he could picture it from the sound alone.

hunks.baseline: The fanatics wavering in shock at this unexpected turn—and the countless forest of spears and blades closing over them.
hunks.sol: The fanatics wavering at this unexpected turn. The forest of countless spears and blades closing over them.

hunks.baseline: The undying will and desperate sense of duty carried by every one of those weapons.
hunks.sol: The unyielding will and desperate sense of duty behind every blade.
“…Why?”

hunks.baseline: The Blood Lord barely managed to squeeze out his voice.
hunks.sol: The Blood Lord barely managed to force out the word.

hunks.baseline: He wanted to ask.
Jin Taekyung. All of them.
hunks.sol: He wanted to ask Jin Taekyung. All of them.

hunks.baseline: What could they possibly hold so dear that they would give their lives to protect it?
hunks.sol: What could they hold so dear that they would give their lives to protect it?

hunks.baseline: Jin Taekyung answered the Blood Lord’s short question, heavy with meaning, with two words even shorter.
hunks.sol: Jin Taekyung answered that short question, laden with meaning, in two even shorter words.

hunks.baseline: “I’m sick of it. It’s not like you’re the first idiot like this I’ve met. I’ve gone out of my way to explain before, and none of you ever understood a damn thing.”
hunks.sol: “I’m sick of it. You’re hardly the first idiot like this I’ve met. I’ve gone out of my way to explain it before, and none of you understood a damn thing.”

hunks.baseline: Jin Taekyung watched the Blood Lord manage a weak nod, then abruptly spoke.
hunks.sol: The Blood Lord managed a weak nod. Jin Taekyung watched him, then asked abruptly, “What about you?”

hunks.baseline: “What about you?”
“You. What the hell were you carrying on for?”
hunks.sol: “What the hell were *you* doing all this for?”

hunks.baseline: The Blood Lord fell silent for a moment, and was startled by his own silence.
hunks.sol: The Blood Lord fell silent for a moment. His own silence startled him.

hunks.baseline: Or was it the feeling of death closing in by the second?
hunks.sol: Or the sense of death drawing closer with every passing second?

hunks.baseline: “……I don’t know.”
hunks.sol: “…I don’t know.”

hunks.baseline: His lips, which should have said that everything he’d done was for the Lord of Heaven—that he would do anything for his great master, and swear his loyalty even if he died here and became a ghost—gave a completely different answer.
hunks.sol: He should have said that everything he’d done was for the Lord of Heaven. That he would do anything for his great master, and would swear loyalty even if he died here and became a ghost.
But the faithful servant’s lips gave a different answer.

hunks.baseline: With that feeble mutter, the Blood Lord looked up at the sky.
hunks.sol: With that faint murmur, the Blood Lord looked up at the sky.

hunks.baseline: Where was the heaven he’d trusted so completely, at this very moment?
hunks.sol: Where was the heaven he had trusted so completely?

hunks.baseline: Would his master, who would hear of the death of his most faithful servant from somewhere far beyond reach, feel even a trace of grief?
hunks.sol: Would his master, somewhere impossibly far away, feel even a trace of grief when he heard that his most faithful servant had died?

hunks.baseline: A faint smile suddenly touched the Blood Lord’s lips.
hunks.sol: A faint smile touched the Blood Lord’s lips.

hunks.baseline: Right.
hunks.sol: Yes.

hunks.baseline: He’d only been trying to deny it. He already knew the answer.
hunks.sol: He had tried to deny it, but he already knew the answer.

hunks.baseline: When the four Demon Lords and the Demon Empress had died one after another, when news came that countless followers had been wiped out, the Lord of Heaven hadn’t wavered.
hunks.sol: The Lord of Heaven hadn’t wavered when the four Demon Lords and the Demon Empress died one after another. Nor when word came that countless followers had been wiped out.

hunks.baseline: He’d acted as though he wanted it to happen.
hunks.sol: It was almost as if he’d wanted it to happen.

hunks.baseline: *Then did you want the death of this lowly servant, too?*
hunks.sol: *Then did you want this lowly servant to die, too?*

hunks.baseline: It was far away. He couldn’t reach it.
hunks.sol: Too far. He couldn’t touch it.

hunks.baseline: Just like the distance between him and the Lord of Heaven.
hunks.sol: Just like the distance between him and the Lord of Heaven. No matter how hard he’d tried, they had never grown any closer.

hunks.baseline: Just like the relationship that had never drawn any closer, no matter how hard he’d tried.
He had believed in and revered the Lord of Heaven—but the light pouring down from that heaven had always shone on only one person.
hunks.sol: He had believed in and revered the Lord of Heaven. But the light pouring down from that heaven had always shone on one person alone.

hunks.baseline: Even though the owner of those blazing eyes could no longer lift a finger, he was watching the Blood Lord die.
hunks.sol: On the owner of those blazing eyes, who could no longer lift a finger yet still watched him die without looking away.

hunks.sol: The fingers that had been reaching desperately through empty air curled like hooks and plunged downward.

hunks.sol: The monster’s final strike carried anger and hatred he no longer knew whom to direct at, and one last duty that now seemed futile.

hunks.sol: Just as it was about to pierce Jin Taekyung between the eyes—

hunks.baseline: A hand, caked in dried blood, blocked the monster’s strike.
hunks.sol: A hand caked in dried blood blocked it.

hunks.baseline: It crushed the bones in the monster’s fingers and burned his flesh and blood.
hunks.sol: The bones in the monster’s fingers shattered, joint by joint, and his flesh and blood burned.

hunks.baseline: A haze rose with the smell of something scorching.
hunks.sol: A haze rose with the smell of scorching flesh.

hunks.baseline: Beyond it, the lips of the old master who had returned to his Disciple’s side parted.
hunks.sol: Beyond it, the old master who had returned to his Disciple’s side parted his lips.

hunks.baseline: Through the heat that pierced even his dulled senses, the Fire King, Jeok Cheongang, looked down at the monster, trembling in pain.
hunks.sol: Through heat that penetrated even his dulled senses, the Fire King, Jeok Cheongang, looked down at the monster trembling in pain.

hunks.baseline: And it wasn’t just him.
hunks.sol: And he wasn’t alone.

hunks.baseline: The Bow Saint and Slaughter Saint. Sword Saint Mae Jonghak and Cheongpung.
hunks.sol: The Bow Saint and the Slaughter Saint. Sword Saint Mae Jonghak and Cheongpung. Others, too, who had rushed over covered in blood.

hunks.baseline: Along with them, several others who had rushed over, covered in blood.
They surrounded him like the God of Death—or an iron tower.
hunks.sol: They surrounded the monster like reapers, like iron towers.

hunks.baseline: Blocking out the entire sky that had been the monster’s whole world.
Becoming a broad, sturdy roof that sheltered someone else from the rain pouring down on them.
hunks.sol: They blotted out the sky that had been his whole world and became a broad, sturdy roof sheltering someone else from the rain.

hunks.baseline: Remembering the monster’s cry of joy just moments ago.
hunks.sol: He remembered the monster’s joyful cry just moments ago.

hunks.baseline: “Can you see?”
hunks.sol: “See them?”

hunks.baseline: He spoke emphatically to the monster, its blood-red eyes wide open.
hunks.sol: He spoke with all the strength he could muster to the monster staring at him with wide, blood-red eyes.

hunks.baseline: “The faces you’re looking at right now—that’s the paltry heaven I believed in.”
hunks.sol: “Those faces you’re looking at? That’s the paltry heaven I believed in.”

hunks.baseline: What could he say?
hunks.sol: What could the monster say?

hunks.baseline: The monster blinked helplessly.
He swallowed the blood that kept spilling over his lips and summoned all his strength to force out the words.
hunks.sol: He blinked helplessly, swallowed the blood spilling over his lips, and forced out a few last words.

hunks.baseline: And through the vision darkening like pitch, Jin Taekyung’s voice rang faintly in his ears.
hunks.sol: As his vision darkened to pitch-black, Jin Taekyung’s voice reached him, faint and distant.

hunks.baseline: As a bitter smile touched Jin Taekyung’s lips, the monster’s final breath dispersed into the air.
hunks.sol: A bitter smile touched Jin Taekyung’s lips. The monster breathed his last, and that breath dispersed into the air.

hunks.baseline: A clear chime rang out like the bells of an ancient cathedral, announcing that everything was over.
hunks.sol: A clear chime rang out like the bell of an ancient cathedral, announcing that everything was over.

hunks.baseline: There’s a saying.
Animals leave their hides behind when they die, and people leave their names.
hunks.sol: There’s a saying: animals leave their hides behind when they die, and people leave their names.

hunks.baseline: But monsters that are neither animal nor human can leave behind a massive amount of EXP.
hunks.sol: But a monster that’s neither animal nor human can leave behind a massive amount of EXP.

hunks.baseline: If everyone could hear it, not just me, I bet it would’ve carried for hundreds of miles.
hunks.sol: If everyone could hear it instead of just me, I bet it would’ve carried for hundreds of miles.

hunks.baseline: *That bastard sure knew how to make an exit.*
hunks.sol: *That bastard sure made an exit.*

hunks.baseline: How many times had I leveled up in that short instant?
hunks.sol: How many times had I leveled up in that brief instant?

hunks.baseline: Three times? More?
hunks.sol: Three? More?

hunks.baseline: What I did know was that several Quests had been completed when the Blood Lord died, and I’d turned off notifications after my third Level Up.
hunks.sol: All I knew was that several Quests had been completed the moment the Blood Lord died, and I’d turned off notifications after my third Level Up.

hunks.baseline: *If this were any other time, I’d have passed out from happiness.*
hunks.sol: *Any other time, I’d have passed out from happiness.*

hunks.baseline: No, I definitely would have.
Leveling up several times in a row, when it had only happened once in a blue moon for a while now, was nothing short of a miracle.
hunks.sol: No, I definitely would have. Leveling up had become a once-in-a-blue-moon event. Doing it several times in a row was nothing short of a miracle.

hunks.baseline: The chimes, which should have sounded like heaven, were nothing but irritating noise. The recovery of my flesh and bones, all crushed and broken, offered only a little comfort.
hunks.sol: The chimes that should have sounded like heaven were just irritating noise. Even having my crushed flesh and broken bones heal offered only a little comfort.

hunks.baseline: The small, final comfort of being able to pat someone’s trembling shoulder.
hunks.sol: One small, final comfort: I could pat someone’s trembling shoulder.

hunks.baseline: Cheongpung didn’t stop crying, despite my attempt to comfort him.
hunks.sol: Cheongpung didn’t stop crying at my attempt to comfort him. He just spoke through his sobs.

hunks.baseline: He could only speak through his sobs.
Saying he was sorry. Saying thanks again.
hunks.sol: He said he was sorry. And thanked me again.

hunks.baseline: But my farewell to Cheongpung, which was surely going to be our last, was brief.
hunks.sol: But my farewell to Cheongpung—surely our last—was brief.

hunks.baseline: Unlike him, I still had so many last faces left to see.
hunks.sol: I still had so many other faces to say goodbye to.

hunks.baseline: And at the end of them, my real final moment would be waiting for me.
hunks.sol: And once I’d seen them all, my own final moment would be waiting.

hunks.baseline: I calmly looked at the hourglass of Final Rally, still suspended in midair.
hunks.sol: I gazed calmly at the hourglass of Final Rally, still hanging in the air.

hunks.baseline: Truthfully, I’d already guessed.
To be precise, ever since the moment I’d launched One Annihilation at the Blood Lord.
hunks.sol: Truthfully, I’d already guessed. Ever since I’d launched One Annihilation at the Blood Lord.

hunks.baseline: There was a limit to how much a Level Up could heal, and the injuries I’d suffered from the backlash of One Annihilation went beyond that limit.
hunks.sol: There was a limit to how much a Level Up could heal, and the injuries I’d suffered from One Annihilation’s backlash went beyond it.

hunks.baseline: Now that what was called innate qi—or original true qi—had been damaged, my fate was like a boat that had crossed a river with no way back.
hunks.sol: With what they called innate qi—or original true qi—damaged, I had crossed a river I could never cross back.

hunks.baseline: *The System warned me, and I accepted it.*
hunks.sol: *The System warned me, and I knew what I was doing.*

hunks.baseline: I’d simply taken the next step I needed to take, even if death was waiting for me.
hunks.sol: I’d taken the step I had to take, even knowing death might be waiting for me.

hunks.baseline: Because I’d already made peace with it, I was even grateful for my situation now.
hunks.sol: I had been prepared for this. If anything, I was grateful for the way things had turned out.

hunks.baseline: If I hadn’t recovered through the Level Ups, if they hadn’t extended the time I had in Final Rally, I wouldn’t have been able to say my final goodbyes like this.
hunks.sol: Without the healing from those Level Ups, without the extra time it had given me in Final Rally, I wouldn’t even have been able to say goodbye.

hunks.baseline: *If that’s what happened, then it was enough.*
hunks.sol: *That’s enough.*

hunks.baseline: The Blood Lord was dead, the Dark Heaven army had crumbled, and I’d been granted a few precious extra minutes.
hunks.sol: The Blood Lord was dead. Dark Heaven’s army had crumbled. And I’d been given a few precious extra minutes.

hunks.baseline: And now I was smiling at faces I’d thought I’d never see again.
hunks.sol: Now I was smiling at faces I’d thought I’d never see again.

hunks.baseline: Like a peaceful day with no enemies left to defeat and no one precious I had to protect.
hunks.sol: As if this were an ordinary, peaceful day, with no enemy to defeat and no one dear to me in need of protection.

hunks.baseline: Just like this moment.
hunks.sol: As if it were just this moment.

hunks.baseline: I definitely had to be.
hunks.sol: I had to be.
